title: Dual Boundary Condition Inference: A Two-Boundary Product Rule and Its Implications
summary: Many inference problems are constrained from two sides: forward information and a second constraint on outcomes. Dual Boundary Condition Inference (DBCI) multiplies them and renormalises. The rule is not new: it is the product-of-experts form and the unit-exponent member of the logarithmic-pooling family. The paper contributes a classification and reducibility characterisation.
